target_customer: Credit funds, fintech lenders, credit unions and banks
problem: Lenders run servicing, collections, underwriting, monitoring and compliance reporting with manual back office work. Levocred builds AI employees that draft IC memos, answer questions on the loan book in Slack and test compliance certificates.
business_model: Usage based AI workforce (company says scale with tokens, not headcount); prices not public
product_category: AI back office automation for lenders

founders.name: Mohit Gupta
prior_employers: Edge Focus Partners (credit fund, per directory)
founders.background_notes: YC page says employee number 1 at a credit fund that grew from $10M to $1B AUM.

founders.name: Saksham Gupta
prior_employers: A credit fund (founding engineer, not named on the YC page)

competitors.name: Antal
competitors.what: Autonomous AI agent stack for private credit, loan file to underwriting ready package

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating with loan tapes, credit agreements and servicer reports and getting accurate cited outputs for finance work is harder than a generic chatbot.

defensibility.rationale: Deep workflow integration helps, but the category has several funded entrants.

market_need_then: Private credit grew and funds need operations staff; a 2026 Apex survey and industry guides discuss AI in private credit operations. Company claims one customer, Pier Asset Management, and $1B+ running through the product (self reported).

branding.domain_note: Uses levocred.com; no purchase details found.

identity.mascot_or_character: Levo, the AI analyst persona introduced August 2026 (per a profile)
identity.voice_and_tone: Human framing of AI: we hired our best analyst, it wasn't human

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive coined name and an analyst persona, but little press about the brand.

outcome_analysis: Levocred is a Summer 2026 company, active, claiming live production use at credit funds. Founders come from credit fund operations, which fits the buyer. No outcome yet; competition from funded private credit AI vendors is the main risk.
notes: Dealroom lists a $125k seed with no date or investors, seen on one aggregator only, so no round is recorded. Customer scale claims conflict: the company site says $1Bn+ runs through it while a directory says about $500M across more than ten facilities. Outcome search found no shutdown or acquisition. Undated competitor sources omitted from the list: Hypercore. Completeness pass: the Dealroom 125K seed is now recorded as a round with no date or investors; it rests on a single database.
